Yellowstone County, Montana property tax involves the county assessment office and the county treasurer.

Who to contact in Yellowstone County

  • Yellowstone County Treasurer
  • Montana Department of Revenue handles assessment and appeals.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • County page states Hank Peters serves as Treasurer, Assessor, and Superintendent of Schools (county-level office; property valuation itself is by state DOR)
  • Real estate: 1st half due November 30 (2026 only: December 3), 2nd half May 31 (2027 only: June 1); mobile home 1st half May 31, 2nd half Nov 30; personal property June 30; all due by 5 PM Mountain Time; weekend/holiday rolls to next business day
  • Delinquent taxes: 2% penalty and 5/6 of 1% interest accumulated monthly (real property, personal, mobile, farm and ranch)
  • Page links online tax payments, tax records search, alternative payment form, tax liens page and property tax protest form; online payments handled by a payment processor
  • Tax records search notes real estate payments accepted (incl. postmark) through Monday June 2 at 5 PM since May 31 was a Saturday (prior-year notice) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • County site links a Tax Appeal Board page (commissioners/taxappeals.asp) and a Property Tax Protest Form (link seen, not opened)

Tax rate

Montana bills combine county, municipal and school district levies.

Selling in Yellowstone County?
We buy Yellowstone County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Recorder not required in this batch

Yellowstone County by the numbers

Yellowstone County ranks 1 of 7 Montana counties in this guide by population, at about 167,340 people in 73,363 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $317,600, the median home value sits 25% below the Montana county median for this guide. The Montana county median income is $71,327, and Yellowstone County reports $74,400. Owner-occupancy is 69%, so renters hold about 31% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1982, about 41 years ago.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • County page lists Department of Revenue (406) 758-5700 as determining taxable value: appraisal, classification, reductions and exemptions
  • Real property: bills printed October, 1st half due Nov 30, 2nd half due May 31; mobile homes bills printed April, 1st half May 31, 2nd half Nov 30; personal property due May & November in most cases
  • Online payment at taxes.flatheadcounty.gov: debit/credit card (3% fee) or eCheck (no fee)
  • Alternative payment schedule for primary residences (MCA 15-16-122): seven monthly payments Nov 30 to May 31; application due September 30 of the tax year
  • 2026 tax bill PDF: 1st installment due by 5:00 p.m. Nov 30, 2nd no later than 5:00 p.m. May 31 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Protest form is for use only after an active appeal with the Department of Revenue; remit payment with form to Flathead County Treasurer, 290 A North Main, Kalispell
